newsitem.title: UK: Cox Insurance buys Christopherson Heath.
newsitem.headline: Cox Insurance buys Christopherson Heath.

text.p: Cox Insurance Holdings Plc said it had agreed to buy Christopherson Heath Group for a maximum 34 million stg, five million stg of which would be deferred and conditional on the achievement of profit targets.
Cox said on Thursday it aimed to raise 38.7 million stg through a placing and open offer of up to 29.33 million shares at 135 pence per share.
Cox said its three largest shareholders who together control 48 percent of the company, had committed to apply for their full entitlements under the open offer.
Christopherson Heath is the managing agency of Syndicate 218, known as Equity Red Star, the largest motor syndicate at Lloyds of London insurance market.
It also operates Boncaster, a registered insurance broker.
It had turnover of 20 million stg in the year ending December 31, 1995 and pretax profits of 4.5 million stg.
Cox Insurance chairman Duncan Clegg said the acquisition should "enhance significantly...earnings per share" in the year ending March 31, 1998.
He said proceeds of the placing and open offer would allow Cox to take advantage of future investment opportunities at Lloyds and to continue expanding its underwriting capacity.
